findings.title: Mutable FIM scan object defeats capture-time and one-use custody
evidence: A genuine completed empty scan returned the exact retained _FIMScanSnapshot.
After scan completion, an inert enrolled marker was created and injected into the mutable mapping and identity dictionary; the mutable receipt counters and snapshot/coverage digests were recomputed.
_evaluate_snapshot accepted the mutated object and minted a version-4 receipt that verify_validation_native_event accepted, even though the file did not exist during the scan.

After one valid evaluation, resetting the snapshot's writable _fim_consumed flag and reinstalling the same object as _pending_scan_snapshot minted a second accepted receipt for the same scan generation.
findings.impact: Same-process code can manufacture native detector credit after scan completion and replay one scan generation for multiple accepted receipts. This affects simulation evidence truth, not host compromise.
findings.recommendation: Keep scan custody in producer-owned state that callers cannot mutate: capture an immutable canonical snapshot/identity/receipt record under a private generation handle, validate the exact current generation, and maintain an issuer-owned consumed-generation set or monotonic claim token. The evaluator should receive only an opaque claim and copied read-only values.

findings.title: Captured verifier closure and live signing key remain module-reachable mutable authority
evidence: The public verify_validation_native_event function exposes verify_native_impl through its writable Python closure cell; replacing cell_contents with a lambda made a receipt-free event pass.

Starting from one valid inert FIM event, changing only event_nonce and recomputing detector_receipt_mac with the reachable key produced a new synthetic Event accepted by verify_validation_native_event.
The sixth author test closes class-attribute replacement but does not exercise closure-cell mutation or registry-reachable key use.
findings.impact: An admitted same-process Python component can redirect validation or mint accepted detector receipts without using the enrolled producer capability. The declared same-process-object-capability label is honest, but the verifier is not immutable and the key is not issuer-only.
findings.recommendation: Do not describe Python closures as immutable. For a security boundary, move signing, replay state, and verification into a measured restricted process/service and expose only opaque handles plus a public verification key. If isolation is deferred, prevent direct state/key return and downgrade the assurance claim to same-process simulation validation.

findings.title: Fixed-head journal continuity and signed handoff
evidence: The exact current report handoff verified normally.
Swapping text, text bytes, or the signed journal row/hash across two authentic report results was rejected.
Dropping the authenticated journal prefix and retaining only row two failed chain validation and invalidated the handoff.
The existing sixth journal-only rollback gate and older signed display replay gates remained green in the 80-test compatibility run.
findings.residual: The remediation already discloses that coordinated rollback of every local witness is not detectable without a separately administered monotonic witness. This re-attack found no narrower rollback or handoff bypass.

supplemental_closure.control: exact producer object and lifecycle generation binding
supplemental_closure.evidence: A valid receipt was rejected after manager module-object replacement and again after lifecycle-generation advance.
A signed duplicate-only, missing-inventory campaign retained detection_steps=13, withheld score eligibility, and emitted a null validation rate.
The existing exact OS-source, generation-bound Process Monitor gate passed unchanged in the broader run.

assurance_boundary: All red reproductions require code already executing in Angerona's Python process and affect Red Team simulation evidence integrity. They use only inert temporary marker files and synthetic events; they do not demonstrate or attempt host compromise.
